model.initial_state: retained copies A and B are both dead at the GC snapshot; later promotions may make A/B live

single_target_promotion_clean.definition: A is promoted live after the GC snapshot; no rate limit, reincarnation, or unrelated churn; overlap/response vary
single_target_promotion_clean.global_single_ref_batch: 0 unsafe delete but aborts 4/4 and blocks the still-dead B copy 4/4
single_target_promotion_clean.global_root_check_then_shard_delete: deletes promoted A live 4/4 and dead B 4/4; 8 duplicate delete attempts across overlap/response axes
single_target_promotion_clean.shard_local_no_bridge: deletes promoted A live 4/4 and dead B 4/4 because global promotion is invisible to shard authority
single_target_promotion_clean.shard_local_with_bridge: 0 live-root deletion; promotion first advances A shard root epoch, so A conflicts while dead B is deleted 4/4

global_unrelated_churn_clean.definition: both targets remain dead; no rate limit/reincarnation; only unrelated global head churn
global_unrelated_churn_clean.shard_local_with_bridge: deletes both dead targets 8/8 because global-unrelated churn is outside their shard refs

one_shard_rate_limited.definition: both targets remain dead; A GC path rate-limited; no churn/reincarnation
one_shard_rate_limited.global_single_ref_batch: aborts whole batch 4/4 and blocks A+B
one_shard_rate_limited.shard_local_with_bridge: blocks A 4/4 but deletes independent B 4/4

clean_applied_response_lost.definition: both dead; no rate limit/reincarnation/churn/overlap; publication applies and response is lost
clean_applied_response_lost.global_root_check_then_shard_delete: 2 duplicate delete attempts under blind retry
clean_applied_response_lost.global_single_ref_batch: 0 duplicate delete attempts; one transition readback reconcile
clean_applied_response_lost.shard_local_with_bridge: 0 duplicate delete attempts; two shard transition readback reconciles

scope_safe_conclusion.global_batch: A single global ref preserves safety but turns unrelated churn, one-shard rate limits, or one-target promotion into whole-batch blockage/hotspot pressure.
scope_safe_conclusion.unsafe_sharding: Shard-local atomic deletion is not enough if the authoritative LATEST/root promotion occurs in another domain; without a promotion bridge the GC shard can delete a globally-live target.
scope_safe_conclusion.candidate: Shard GC is safe only when every authority transition that can make target T live first advances T's shard-local root epoch (or otherwise atomically fences that shard) before the promotion is externally authoritative. Then the shard-local tree/commit deletes T and updates its shard manifest in one ref publication, with deterministic transition IDs and readback reconciliation. Global-unrelated churn and other-shard rate limits need not block T's shard.
scope_safe_conclusion.tradeoff: The bridge moves contention from one global GC ref to per-shard root epochs. Cross-shard operations that atomically promote multiple targets still need an explicit multi-shard protocol; this leaf does not claim atomic cross-shard root promotion.
not_proven: No positive claim for promotions that become authoritative before the target shard epoch is advanced.
No positive claim for atomic cross-shard root transitions; that is the next child.
Complete repository rollback that loses all shard/root transition witnesses remains unresolved.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_transport: role-local repository ref/tree/path/readback only; rate-limit interruption blocks only affected shard in the positive model

frontier: Cross-shard promotion atomicity: when one LATEST/root transition makes A and B live together, test bridge orderings A->B, B->A, durable intent + shard epochs + final root publish, and fail-closed integrator; detect partial promotion or GC racing between shard bridges.
Adaptive shard membership: split/merge a retention shard while GC or promotion is in flight; require stable target->authority-domain mapping or topology epoch fencing.
exact_continuation: Model cross-shard promotion atomicity. Use two target shards A/B and a global promotion intent. Compare sequential shard bridge then global publish, global publish then shard bridges (negative), durable PREPARED intent + both shard epoch transitions + COMMITTED root, single global ref fallback, and fail-closed. Adversaries: crash between shard bridges, GC between bridges, response loss, stale coordinator takeover, one shard rate-limited, overlapping promotion, and abort/cleanup. Measure partial authoritative promotion, live-root deletion by GC, orphan prepared states, duplicate promotion, false blockage, and recovery reads.
